checks: Pure vs ambient type discipline (claim 1). A is K4/I5-free on 18 vertices; the note explicitly does NOT assume A I4-free, and the proof needs only that H = A-({u} union N_A(u)) is I4-free. I re-derived this: u's neighbors in A are exactly S, so u is anticomplete to H, hence any I4 in H together with u is an I5 in A; K4-freeness of H is heredity. The eight-neighbor cap is then sound: S is triangle-free (a triangle with u gives K4, so Mantel gives e(S)<=floor(s^2/4)); for z in S the induced graph on N_H(z) is triangle-free (triangle plus z is K4) and I4-free as an induced subgraph of H, so R(3,4)=9 forces |N_H(z)|<=8 and e(S,H)<=8s (each S-H edge counted at its S-endpoint).

Edge partition and ceilings (claim 1). A is the disjoint union {u}, S, H with no u-H edges, so a = s + e(S) + e(S,H) + e(H) exactly. With the recorded caps U(17..13) = 68,60,55,50,45 I recomputed U(17-s)+9s+floor(s^2/4) for s=0..4: 68+0+0=68, 60+9+0=69, 55+18+1=74, 50+27+2=79, 45+36+4=85. The note's caps 68,69,74,79,85 are exact, and because each bound is the maximum over all s' <= s, the strict thresholds a>68, a>69, a>74, a>79 yield s>=1,2,3,4 respectively. Direction check: for n=13,14,15 the README max column is an upper bound on the extremum (open intervals 33..45, 41..50, 50..55), which is exactly the direction a cap needs; n=16,17 are recorded exact (60..60, 68..68).

Independent deletion bound and the L(q) table (claim 1). A-u is an induced (4,5)-free graph on 17 vertices with e(A-u)=a-s, so the recorded E(4,5,17)<=79 gives s>=a-79=6-q, and 0 bounds it below. I recomputed max(0, 6-q, cap-forced floor) for every q=0..35 from a=85-q: the boundary cases are q=5 (a=80>79 forces s>=4 although 6-q=1), q=6 (a=79 is not >79, caps give only s>=3), q=10 (a=75>74 gives 3), q=11 (a=74 not >74, s>=2 from a=74>69... precisely s<=1 caps at 69<74), q=15 (a=70>69 gives 2), q=16 (a=69>68 gives 1), q=17 (a=68, no cap applies, 6-q<0, so L=0). The resulting table is exactly 6,5,4 at q=0,1,2; 4 at q=3..5; 3 at q=6..10; 2 at q=11..15; 1 at q=16; 0 at q=17..35, matching the note line-for-line, and the stated a-form (L=0 at a<=68, 1 at 69, 2 at 70..74, 3 at 75..79, 4 at 80..83, 5 at 84, 6 at 85) is the same function re-parameterized. The connected clause is elementary (a connected graph on more than one vertex has minimum degree at least 1) and is clearly conditional, not part of the pure scope.

Ceiling derivation (claim 2). Both bounds check: A-u is (4,5)-free on 17 vertices with e=a-d_A(u), and the recorded min e(4,5,17)=41 is a lower bound for every (4,5)-free graph on 17 vertices (independently, the README min column equals C(17,2)-E(5,4,17)=136-95=41 under complementation, and this identity holds in every row of the README table, e.g. 91-69=22, 276-132=144 - the same reading under which the accepted e(B)>=144 premise operates). Hence d_A(u)<=a-41=44-q. Second bound: N_A(u) is triangle-free (triangle with u gives K4) and I5-free (heredity), so R(3,5)=14 gives d_A(u)<=13. D(q)=min(13,44-q) therefore, and D<13 iff q>=32 iff a in 50..53 with values 12,11,10,9 at q=32,33,34,35, exactly as concluded; for q<=31 the bound 44-q>=13 is slack. The improvement claim (cap13 tightened precisely at a=50..53, no connectivity or cross-count hypothesis) is correct.

Row identity and row-inequality directions (claim 3). For u in A: d_G(u)=1+d_A(u)+r_u (pivot v, A-neighbors, B-neighbors), so r_u=17+epsilon_u-d_A(u). Substituting L<=d_A(u)<=D flips correctly on both sides: 17+epsilon-D <= r_u <= 17+epsilon-L; intersecting with the recorded r_u<=17 and r_u>=0 gives max(0,17+epsilon-D)<=r_u<=min(17,17+epsilon-L). Direction of every inequality verified. Consequences re-derived: r_u<=17 implies d_A(u)>=epsilon_u; r_u=17 together with r_u<=17+epsilon-L forces epsilon_u>=L; at L=4 (q=2..5) size-17 rows are excluded at excess 0..3. Consistency with the accepted combined-pairs fact (size-17 row has d_u=epsilon_u) holds: the two give epsilon_u=d_u>=L. Also D(q)>=6>=L(q)+... in particular L(q)<=D(q) for all q (L<=6<=9<=D), so no row bound is vacuously contradictory.

Actual-multiplicity averaging (claim 3, bullet 2). The 18 A-vertices partition into t=m_0 vertices at excess 0 and sum_{i=1..6} m_i vertices at excess i, with sum_i m_i=18. Handshake: total interior degree is 2a=170-2q. Each excess-i vertex satisfies d_A>=max(L,i): the L half is claim 1 (pure scope covers ambient A), the i half is the row identity with r_u<=17 (d_A=17+epsilon-r>=epsilon=i). Therefore the t excess-zero vertices carry total at most 170-2q-sum_{i>=1} m_i max(L,i), some one carries at most the average, its overlap with v is exactly lambda_vu=|N(v) cap N(u)|=N_A(u)=d_A(u), and claim 2 caps every vertex by D. The stated quotient and the min with D follow. The hypothesis t>0 is exactly what the division needs and is explicitly stated (in contrast to bullet 3, where it is derived).

E-only simplification, monotonic substitution (claim 3, bullet 3). z=sum_{i>0} m_i <= sum_{i>0} i*m_i = E because each i>=1, and z<=E<=17 gives t=18-z>=1 (denominator positive, t>0 derived as claimed). The previous average is at most f(z)=(170-2q-Lz)/(18-z) since sum m_i max(L,i)>=Lz. f'(z) has the sign of 170-2q-18L: I checked this quantity for every q=0..35 against the proved L(q); its minimum over all q is 62 (at q=0), so f is increasing everywhere it is used; equivalently 170-2q is the actual handshake total and 18L is the floor on it, so the nonnegativity is a necessary consequence as the note says. Since z<=E<18 and f increasing, f(z)<=f(E); lambda is an integer so lambda<=floor(f(E)), combined with D. I verified f(q,z)<=f(E) numerically for all q in 0..35 and all 0<=z<=E<=17 with zero violations.

Concrete transfers q4E4, q5E8, q10E4. Old values reproduce pivot_classes section 2 exactly with L_old=max(0,6-q): min(13,floor((170-8-2*4)/14))=min(13,11)=11; min(13,floor((170-10-1*8)/10))=min(13,15)=13; min(13,floor((170-20-0)/14))=min(13,10)=10. New values with L(q)=4,4,3: min(13,floor((170-8-16)/14))=min(13,10)=10; min(13,floor((170-10-32)/10))=min(13,12)=12; min(13,floor((170-20-12)/14))=min(13,9)=9. All three pairs (11->10, 13->12, 10->9) match the note. Each example satisfies E<=17 (so bullet 3 applies and t>=18-E>0) and D(q)=13 is non-binding at q=4,5,10.

Census directions (all claims). E(4,4,n) upper caps for H: correct direction (recorded max column). E(4,5,17)<=79 upper: correct for s>=a-79. min e(4,5,17)=41 lower: correct for e(A-u)>=41, and I verified the README min column equals C(n,2) minus the complementary max in all thirteen rows, so it is a bound over all graphs in R(s,t,n) in the README's own semantics, matching the note's premise '41<=e(4,5,17)'. R(3,4)=9 to |N_H(z)|<=8: correct orientation (no K3 and no I4). R(3,5)=14 to d_A<=13: correct. R(4,5)=25 with baseline line 30 (n-25<=d(v)<=24, n=43) to 18<=d_G<=24 and epsilon in [0,6]: correct. Source attributions for the (4,4) and (4,5,17) edge rows (McKay-Radziszowski 1992 [2], Angeltveit-McKay [1]) verified against the README references; the finer 'Appendix A Table 1' attribution matches existing in-repo usage (pivot_classes, transfer_bounds, four_column_stability, pairwise_frontier_refinements) and was not rechecked against the paper (no downloads permitted).

Comparison with the old pivot_classes formulas. Recomputed L(q) against old max(0,6-q) for all q: strictly larger exactly at q=3..16 and equal at q=0..2 and q=17..35, so 'strictly strengthened for every q=3..16' is exact, and the three advertised instances check (a=82: 4 vs 3; a=80: 4 vs 1; a=75: 3 vs 0). D=min(13,44-q)<=13 pointwise, strictly smaller exactly at q>=32 (a=50..53). For the pointed filters, new caps are <= old caps at every one of the 36x18 (q,E<=17) pairs (zero regressions) and strictly smaller at 63 pairs, so the old formulas are genuinely strengthened, not merely re-derived. The stated limit also holds: over all six W=0,2,4,6,8,10 rows I reproduced the published old per-q lists exactly from the old formula and found the per-W worst-case guarantees unchanged (9,9,10,11,12,12); individual interior entries do improve (e.g. W=8 at q=4: 11->10, W=10 at q=3: 12->11), so 'the worst-case W<=10 overlap table need not improve' is accurate for the table as published.

Quantifiers and scope discipline (claim 3). The chosen vertex is always an A-neighbor u of v with epsilon_u=0 (a degree-18 root); the note correctly warns that this companion root need not share q or E with v, and no selected-root equality, profile occurrence, worst-case table improvement, or d18 exclusion is claimed (limits field). Bullet 2 requires t>0 and states it; bullet 3 derives it from E<=17. If the simplified numerator were negative the profile itself would be contradictory (sum of t degrees >= t*L >= 0), so the bound is never falsely asserted for realizable profiles. Claim 1 and 2 use no E or x hypothesis (scope fields accurate); claim 3 uses only the pure claims, the recorded row facts, and handshake arithmetic - no census beyond what the setting declares. parameter_landscape (unaccepted) is not used anywhere.

Notation observation (non-blocking). The symbol U in 'the recorded maximum U(17-s)' is never defined in the note; the stated caps 68,69,74,79,85 pin U(17..13)=68,60,55,50,45 uniquely, which is exactly README max E(4,4,13..17). I recorded the intended reading; no proof content depends on anything beyond those five numbers.
